edits.old: For reads of sharded collections on secondary shard nodes, available avoids waiting for routing-table cache refreshes that local may require. This can reduce latency and tolerate metadata-service partitions, but stale routing can expose orphaned documents or an obsolete chunk view. (high confidence)
edits.new: For sharded clusters, read concern "available" provides greater tolerance for partitions: queries do not require a check that the correct shard received them and, unlike "local", do not contact the shard's primary or the config servers for updated metadata. The trade-off is that queries may return orphaned documents during chunk migration, and the receiving shard may not be the authoritative owner of the requested data. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md ; https://www.php.net/mongodb-driver-readconcern

edits.old: To request this level explicitly, supported read commands use readConcern: { level: "available" }; the client URI option readConcernLevel controls the default read concern and is separate from readPreference, which controls server selection. (high confidence)
edits.new: The client URI option readConcernLevel defines the level for the read concern, and read preference is a separate setting that describes how clients route reads to replica set members. Read concern is specified as readConcern: { level: ... }, and "available" is a supported level. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/read-write-concern/read-write-concern.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md
